questions.question: When was the rolling plan adopted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**After the fifth five-year plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Rolling Plan** was introduced after the termination of the **Fifth Five-Year Plan** in **1978** by the **Janata Party Government**.
 
• The concept of the Rolling Plan was aimed to replace the fixed five-year plans with a flexible annual plan that could be revised based on the country's economic performance and requirements.
 
• It was initiated under the leadership of **Morarji Desai**, who served as the Prime Minister of India during that period.
 
• This plan was designed to provide greater flexibility to policymaking, ensuring that the government could adapt to changing economic conditions without being constrained by the rigid framework of a fixed-term plan.
 
• The **Rolling Plan** was eventually abandoned, and the Sixth Five-Year Plan was introduced in **1980** under the Congress government led by **Indira Gandhi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Five-Year Plans in India:**

 
 
• The concept of Five-Year Plans was introduced in India in **1951** inspired by the **Soviet Union's planning model**.
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan (1951-56)** focused on agricultural development and infrastructure building.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61)** emphasized industrialization and the development of heavy industries.
 
• Subsequent plans had specific objectives, such as poverty alleviation, employment generation, and sustainable growth.
 
 
 
• **Janata Party's Economic Policy:**
 
 
• The Janata Party, under **Morarji Desai's leadership**, sought to modify the planning process by introducing the Rolling Plan concept.
 
• This approach was designed to align economic priorities with the actual outcomes and adjust the policies dynamically.
 
• The government emphasized decentralization and reducing state control over industries and businesses during this period.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of Rolling Plan:**
 
 
• The Rolling Plan faced criticism for lacking long-term vision and consistency in policy-making.
 
• Frequent revisions led to confusion and inefficiencies in implementation.
 
• The Congress government, upon returning to power in **1980**, decided to revert to the traditional Five-Year Plan structure.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• During the late **1970s**, India was undergoing significant economic and political changes, including the Emergency period (1975-77).
 
• The Janata Party's policies reflected its commitment to democracy, decentralization, and liberalization of the economy.
 
• However, the lack of coherence and long-term planning under the Rolling Plan contributed to its failure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Planning Commission:**

 
 
• Established in **1950**, the Planning Commission was responsible for creating and overseeing Five-Year Plans in India.
 
• It was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** in **2015** under the Modi government.
 
 
 
• **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-85):**
 
 
• This plan marked the return to fixed-term planning after the failure of the Rolling Plan.
 
• It focused on poverty alleviation, employment creation, and economic modernization.
 
• It was successful in achieving a growth rate of **5.7%**, which exceeded its target.
 
 
 
• **Flexible Planning:**
 
 
• While the Rolling Plan was abandoned, the idea of flexible planning influenced later approaches to economic policy-making in India.
 
• It highlighted the importance of adapting policies to changing circumstances and economic realities.

questions.question:
Identify the correct statement(s) from the following with reference to 2023-24 Union Budget of the Government of India.

i. The outlay for PM Awas Yojana is being enhanced to over ₹79,000 crores.

ii. The targeted agriculture credit is ₹20 lakh crores.

iii. The Government has targeted to provide central assistance of approximately ₹10,000 crores to the drought-prone central region of Karnataka.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement i:** The **outlay for PM Awas Yojana** has been enhanced to over **₹79,000 crores**. This is correct, as the Union Budget 2023-24 allocated this increased funding to provide housing for all under the flagship scheme.
 
• **Statement ii:** The **targeted agriculture credit** for 2023-24 is set at **₹20 lakh crores**. This is accurate, as the government aims to boost agricultural productivity and support farmers through institutional credit.
 
• **Statement iii:** The government has targeted central assistance of approximately **₹10,000 crores** to the drought-prone central region of Karnataka. This statement is incorrect, as the Union Budget 2023-24 did not specifically mention such a targeted allocation for Karnataka.
 
• **Correct Option:** Since statements i and ii are correct, the correct answer is Option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **PM Awas Yojana:**

 
 
• Launched in **2015**, this scheme aims to provide affordable housing to urban and rural poor by 2022.
 
• The enhanced allocation of ₹79,000 crores in the 2023-24 budget highlights the government’s commitment to achieving the "Housing for All" mission.
 
• The scheme includes both **PMAY-Urban** and **PMAY-Gramin** segments for holistic development.
 
 
 
• **Targeted Agriculture Credit:**
 
 
• The ₹20 lakh crores target for agriculture credit is designed to provide financial support to farmers and agricultural enterprises for better productivity.
 
• The credit allocation includes loans for animal husbandry, dairy, and fisheries sectors.
 
• This initiative also supports digital public infrastructure for agriculture and boosts the adoption of sustainable practices.
 
 
 
• **Union Budget 2023-24 Highlights:**
 
 
• **Capital investment** was increased by 33% to ₹10 lakh crores, representing 3.3% of GDP.
 
• Focus on green growth initiatives, including energy transition and climate action.
 
• Promotion of **inclusive development**, aiming to support sectors such as education, healthcare, and agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Drought-Prone Area Allocation:**
 
 
• While the budget focuses on addressing climate resilience and drought mitigation, no specific ₹10,000 crore allocation to Karnataka was announced.
 
• Programs such as the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) aim to mitigate drought impacts across India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **PM Awas Yojana:**

 
 
• Eligibility includes economically weaker sections (EWS), low-income groups, and middle-income groups.
 
• The scheme provides subsidies on interest rates for home loans and ensures access to basic amenities.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture Credit:**
 
 
• Includes interest subvention schemes for farmers to reduce the financial burden.
 
• Promotes digitization in agriculture by supporting startups and agri-tech firms.
 
 
 
• **Union Budget Objectives:**
 
 
• Aligns with **Amrit Kaal** vision for India’s development by 2047.
 
• Focus on infrastructure, education, healthcare, and economic growth.
 
• Encourages participation in global supply chains through initiatives like the **PLI scheme**.

questions.question: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor?
questions.solution:

• The **Governor** of a state in India is administered the oath of office by the **Chief Justice of the High Court** of that respective state.
 
• This process is outlined under **Article 159** of the **Indian Constitution**, which provides details regarding the oath or affirmation taken by the Governor.
 
• The oath emphasizes allegiance to the Constitution of India and ensures the Governor’s commitment to discharging their duties faithfully and impartially.
 
• If the Chief Justice of the High Court is unavailable, the oath may be administered by the **senior-most judge of the High Court** as per constitutional provisions.
 
• This formal process is crucial for the Governor to officially assume their role and exercise their constitutional powers.

questions.question: Aligned with the objective of state control over vital sectors of the economy, the Industrial Policy of Resolution of 1956 was enacted, serving as the foundation for the ___________ Five Year Plan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**second**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956** was a landmark policy document in India that aimed to strengthen the role of the state in controlling critical sectors of the economy. It emphasized the establishment of a socialist pattern of society by encouraging the public sector to play a dominant role.
 
• This resolution prioritized the allocation of resources to industries of strategic importance, such as defense, atomic energy, and heavy industries, under the direct control of the government.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)**, formulated under the leadership of **Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru** and guided by economist **Dr. P.C. Mahalanobis**, was heavily influenced by the principles outlined in the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956.
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan focused on the development of capital goods industries, such as iron and steel, heavy engineering, and machine-building, aligning with the goal of state control over vital economic sectors.
 
• The resolution and the plan together aimed to create a balanced and self-reliant economy by prioritizing industrialization as a key driver of economic growth, poverty reduction, and modernization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956:**

 
 
• The resolution divided industries into three categories:
 
 
• **Category 1:** Industries exclusively under state control, such as arms and ammunition, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• **Category 2:** Industries where the state would play a dominant role but private sector participation was allowed, including machine tools, fertilizers, and chemicals.
 
• **Category 3:** Industries left for private sector operation, with the state providing necessary support.
 
 
 
• The resolution aimed to reduce regional disparities by promoting industrial development in less developed regions.
 
• It emphasized the importance of small-scale industries to complement large-scale industries.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan:**
 
 
• It was based on the **Mahalanobis model**, which emphasized heavy industries and capital goods production.
 
• The plan allocated substantial resources to the establishment of public sector enterprises like Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (**BHEL**) and Steel Authority of India (**SAIL**).
 
• This plan marked the beginning of planned industrial development with a focus on self-reliance.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• The First Plan (1951-1956) focused on agriculture and irrigation to recover from the partition's aftermath.
 
• The Second Plan emphasized industrialization as a key tool for economic development.
 
• Subsequent plans built upon the foundation laid by the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Industrial Policy Resolution:**
 
 
• It laid the groundwork for India’s industrial policy and its focus on public sector-led growth.
 
• It helped establish institutions like the **National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC)** to support small-scale industries.
 
• The policy was instrumental in creating a mixed economy with both public and private sector participation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Planned Economy:** India adopted the concept of **Five-Year Plans** inspired by the Soviet Union to achieve economic development in a systematic manner.
 
• **Role of Public Sector:** The resolution emphasized the expansion of the public sector to ensure equitable distribution of resources and economic stability.
 
• **Balanced Regional Development:** It aimed to reduce regional disparities through targeted investment in backward areas.
 
• **Legacy:** The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 continues to be a significant milestone in shaping India's economic policies and industrial development strategy.

questions.question: In the 'Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana', the loan cover for Shishu category is upto _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹50,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)** was launched by the Government of India in **April 2015** to provide financial support to micro and small enterprises.
 
• Under PMMY, loans are categorized into three types based on the amount: **Shishu**, **Kishor**, and **Tarun**.
 
• The **Shishu category** provides loans up to **₹50,000** to support small-scale business activities such as startups or enterprises requiring minimal capital. This is the correct answer.
 
• The **Kishor category** covers loans ranging from **₹50,001 to ₹5,00,000**, aimed at enterprises in the growth phase.
 
• The **Tarun category** provides loans ranging from **₹5,00,001 to ₹10,00,000**, targeting businesses seeking to expand operations or scale up.
 
• These loans are collateral-free and are issued by banks, NBFCs, and MFIs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Purpose of PMMY:**

 
 
• The scheme aims to promote entrepreneurship and self-employment among individuals, especially in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
• It focuses on promoting the economic empowerment of **women** and marginalized sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• Any Indian citizen with a viable business plan for manufacturing, trading, or service activities can apply for loans under PMMY.
 
• Applicants must not have any prior loan defaults and should meet the financial institution’s criteria.
 
 
 
• **Loan Coverage:**
 
 
• Loans are provided for a variety of purposes, including setting up shops, purchasing equipment, and starting small businesses.
 
• These loans do not require collateral, making them accessible to small entrepreneurs.
 
 
 
• **Features of PMMY:**
 
 
• The interest rates are determined by the lending institutions, but they are generally lower than commercial rates.
 
• Repayment tenure can go up to **5 years**.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• Since its launch, PMMY has supported millions of micro and small businesses in India, contributing significantly to job creation and economic growth.
 
• It has empowered people from **economically weaker sections** by providing access to credit.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA):**

 
 
• MUDRA was established as a **subsidiary of SIDBI** to regulate and refinance microfinance institutions.
 
• Its primary aim is to provide financial support to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Funding Sources:**
 
 
• Loans under PMMY are funded by banks, NBFCs, and MFIs, with refinancing support from MUDRA.
 
• MUDRA extends refinance support to these institutions at concessional rates.
 
 
 
• **MUDRA Card:**
 
 
• MUDRA Card is a **debit card** issued under PMMY, which enables borrowers to withdraw funds from ATMs or make digital payments.
 
• It is linked to the borrower’s account, ensuring easy access to credit.
 
 
 
• **Achievements:**
 
 
• Since its inception, PMMY has disbursed loans worth **billions of rupees**, benefiting over **30 crore beneficiaries** across India.
 
• It has played a crucial role in fostering a culture of **self-reliance** and entrepreneurship.

questions.question: In 2021, Dr. Padmaja Suresh was awarded the title of 'Karnataka Kalashree' for her best performance in which dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dr. **Padmaja Suresh** was honored with the prestigious title of **'Karnataka Kalashree'** in **2021** for her excellence and contribution to the classical dance form **Bharatanatyam**.
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest and most revered forms of Indian classical dance, originating in **Tamil Nadu**. It is deeply rooted in the **Natya Shastra**, an ancient Sanskrit treatise on performing arts.
 
• As a renowned dancer, Dr. Padmaja Suresh has dedicated her life to preserving and promoting **Indian classical dance**, especially Bharatanatyam, through performances, workshops, and academic engagements.
 
• The **'Karnataka Kalashree'** title is awarded to individuals who have significantly contributed to the field of arts, culture, and heritage in Karnataka.
 
• Dr. Padmaja Suresh's recognition highlights her immense talent, dedication, and contribution to the preservation and propagation of **Bharatanatyam** as an art form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• **Origin:** Bharatanatyam is believed to have originated more than 2,000 years ago in **South India**, particularly in temples of Tamil Nadu.
 
• **Philosophy:** It is deeply connected to **spiritual themes**, portraying stories from Hindu mythology and expressing devotion to deities such as **Lord Shiva, Vishnu, and Krishna**.
 
• **Technique:** This dance form incorporates complex footwork, graceful hand gestures (**mudras**), and intricate facial expressions (**abhinaya**) to convey emotions and narratives.
 
• **Structure:** A Bharatanatyam performance is divided into several segments, including **Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Varnam, Tillana**, and **Padams**. Each segment showcases different aspects of rhythm, expression, and storytelling.
 
• **Costume:** The dancers wear traditional attire consisting of colorful silk sarees, adorned with intricate jewelry and expressive makeup, including exaggerated eye designs.
 
 
 
• **Karnataka Kalashree Award:**
 
 
• This award is presented by the **Karnataka Government** to individuals excelling in various forms of art, culture, and heritage.
 
• It recognizes contributions to fields such as **classical music, dance, theater, literature**, and visual arts.
 
• The recipients of the award are celebrated for their efforts in promoting and preserving the cultural traditions of **Karnataka and India**.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian Classical Dance Forms:**
 
 
• **Mohiniattam:** Originating from **Kerala**, this dance form is known for its graceful movements and feminine charm, often revolving around themes of love and devotion.
 
• **Kathak:** A classical dance form from **North India**, characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and storytelling through gestures and facial expressions.
 
• **Sattriya:** Originating in **Assam**, it was introduced by the saint **Srimanta Sankardeva** and is traditionally performed in monasteries as a form of devotional expression.
 
 
 
• **Natya Shastra:**
 
 
• It is an ancient Sanskrit text attributed to the sage **Bharata**, considered the foundation of Indian classical dances.
 
• The text outlines the principles, postures, gestures, and techniques of performing arts, including dance, drama, and music.
 
• It serves as the basis for the classical dance forms of India, including **Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, and Odissi**.

questions.question: What can be used to sanitise water in swimming pools?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bleaching powder**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bleaching powder**, chemically known as **calcium hypochlorite**, is widely used to sanitize water in swimming pools. It acts as a disinfectant by killing bacteria, viruses, and other pathogens present in the water.
 
• Bleaching powder releases **chlorine** when dissolved in water, which effectively destroys microorganisms and ensures the water is safe for swimming.
 
• It helps prevent the spread of waterborne diseases, such as **cryptosporidiosis** and **giardiasis**, which can occur through contaminated pool water.
 
• This compound is highly effective, affordable, and easy to use, making it a preferred choice for pool maintenance worldwide.
 
• Swimming pool operators often monitor the chlorine levels regularly to ensure proper sanitization and maintain the safety and hygiene of the pool water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Bleaching Powder:**

 
 
• Bleaching powder is a white or light yellow powder with a strong chlorine smell.
 
• It is soluble in water, and its effectiveness depends on its chlorine content.
 
• Commonly used not only for swimming pools but also for disinfecting drinking water, cleaning surfaces, and bleaching fabrics.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Washing soda:** While washing soda (sodium carbonate) is used for cleaning purposes, it is not suitable for sanitizing water as it does not have disinfectant properties.
 
• **Dettol:** Dettol is a liquid antiseptic used for personal hygiene and cleaning wounds but is not appropriate for sanitizing large volumes of water like swimming pools.
 
• **Caustic soda:** Caustic soda (sodium hydroxide) is a strong base used in industrial cleaning but does not have disinfectant capabilities for water treatment.
 
 
 
• **Safety Measures:**
 
 
• Bleaching powder should be handled with care as it can irritate the skin, eyes, and respiratory system.
 
• Proper dosage is essential to avoid excessive chlorine levels, which can lead to health issues like skin irritation and eye redness.
 
 
 
• **Global Usage:**
 
 
• Bleaching powder is widely used worldwide for water sanitation, especially in developing countries where access to advanced water treatment systems is limited.
 
• It is a critical component in emergency relief efforts to purify water during natural disasters and public health crises.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chlorine Chemistry:** Chlorine, released from bleaching powder, kills microorganisms by reacting with their cellular components, disrupting essential processes for survival.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** Excessive chlorine usage can lead to the formation of harmful by-products like **trihalomethanes (THMs)** in water, which can pose risks to human health and the environment.
 
• **Monitoring Pool Water:** Regular testing of chlorine levels and pH is essential to ensure the pool water remains safe and comfortable for swimmers.
 
• **Storage of Bleaching Powder:** It should be stored in a cool, dry place away from moisture to prevent degradation and loss of effectiveness.

questions.question: When did India host the Asian Games for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Asian Games** were hosted by **India for the first time in 1951**. This was a landmark event in the history of Indian sports.
 
• The games were held in **New Delhi, India**. It marked the debut of the Asian Games as a continental multi-sport event.
 
• The inaugural Asian Games were conducted under the aegis of the **Asian Games Federation**, with the participation of **11 nations** and over **490 athletes**.
 
• The event featured **six sports disciplines**, including athletics, aquatics, basketball, cycling, football, and weightlifting.
 
• The opening ceremony took place at the **National Stadium in New Delhi**, with the then Prime Minister of India, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, formally inaugurating the games.
 
• The 1951 Asian Games symbolized the unity and cooperation among Asian nations and set the stage for subsequent editions of the games.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Asian Games History:**

 
 
• The Asian Games, also known as **Asiad**, are a continental multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from across Asia.
 
• The concept of the Asian Games was initiated by the **Asian Games Federation** in 1949, with the first games held in 1951.
 
• The Asian Games are governed by the **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)**, which oversees the event's organization and management.
 
• The games aim to foster unity and friendship among Asian nations through sports.
 
 
 
• **India's Role in the Asian Games:**
 
 
• India was the first host country of the Asian Games, showcasing its commitment to promoting international sports.
 
• India has hosted the Asian Games twice: **1951 and 1982**, both in New Delhi.
 
• India has been an active participant in the Asian Games, winning numerous medals across various disciplines.
 
 
 
• **Key Facts about the 1951 Asian Games:**
 
 
• The games had **11 participating nations**, including Afghanistan, Burma (Myanmar), Indonesia, Iran, Japan, Nepal, Philippines, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Thailand, and India.
 
• A total of **169 events** were held in the six sports categories.
 
• India finished second in the medal tally, winning **15 gold medals**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of the Asian Games:**
 
 
• The Asian Games have grown significantly in scale over the years, with more countries and participants joining each edition.
 
• The most recent Asian Games were held in **Hangzhou, China**, in 2023, featuring 45 nations and thousands of athletes.
 
• The games now include a wide variety of sports, ranging from traditional events like athletics to newer sports such as esports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Asian Games:**

 
 
• The Asian Games serve as a platform for cultural exchange and unity among Asian nations.
 
• It offers athletes from diverse backgrounds the opportunity to compete internationally and showcase their talent.
 
• The event contributes to the development of sports infrastructure and promotes physical fitness and sportsmanship.
 
 
 
• **India's Achievements:**
 
 
• India consistently performs well at the Asian Games, particularly in athletics, shooting, and wrestling.
 
• Indian athletes have earned global recognition through their performance in the Asian Games.
 
• The event has inspired many young athletes in India to pursue sports as a career.
 
 
 
• **Future of the Asian Games:**
 
 
• The Asian Games continue to expand, incorporating new sports and events to stay relevant with global trends.
 
• Efforts are being made to enhance the inclusivity of the games by introducing events for disabled athletes.
 
• The games are a crucial step toward achieving greater cooperation and understanding among Asian countries.

questions.question: Bhupinder Singh was awarded Sangeet Natak Akademi award in 2015 for which of the following musical traditions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sugam Sangeet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhupinder Singh** was awarded the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in **2015** for his contributions to **Sugam Sangeet**, which is a genre of light classical music that blends traditional and modern elements.
 
• Sugam Sangeet refers to the genre of music that encompasses light classical music forms, including **ghazals, bhajans, patriotic songs, folk songs**, and other semi-classical music styles.
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi** Awards are presented annually by the Government of India to recognize individuals' achievements in performing arts, including music, dance, and drama.

• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards:**

questions.question: When trapped water in an aquifer is surrounded by layers of impermeable rock or clay, which apply positive pressure to the water, it is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Artesian Aquifer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An **artesian aquifer** is a confined aquifer containing groundwater under positive pressure.
 
• It is surrounded by layers of **impermeable rock or clay** that prevent water from escaping, creating pressure.
 
• When water is tapped in an artesian aquifer, it rises above the top of the aquifer without the need for pumping, due to the **hydrostatic pressure**.
 
• This phenomenon occurs because the aquifer is sandwiched between impermeable layers and receives water from a higher elevation, allowing it to maintain positive pressure.
 
• Such aquifers are often used as a reliable source of groundwater for irrigation, municipal water supply, and industrial purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Unconfined Aquifer:**

 
 
• An unconfined aquifer is not bounded by impermeable layers, and the water table is exposed to atmospheric pressure.
 
• The water level in wells tapping this aquifer corresponds to the water table level, and pumping is required to extract water.
 
• These aquifers are susceptible to contamination from surface pollutants because of their open nature.
 
 
 
• **Unsaturated Aquifer:**
 
 
• The unsaturated zone, also known as the vadose zone, is located above the water table and contains both air and water within soil pores.
 
• It is not a reliable source of water extraction as it lacks saturation.
 
• This zone serves as a transit layer for water moving downward towards saturated aquifers.
 
 
 
• **Perched Aquifer:**
 
 
• A perched aquifer is formed above the main water table due to a localized impermeable layer (like clay) preventing water from draining downward.
 
• It is smaller and less reliable compared to other aquifer types.
 
• Such aquifers are often temporary and may disappear during dry periods.
 
 
 
• **Artesian Aquifer Characteristics:**
 
 
• These aquifers have **high pressure**, enabling water to flow to the surface naturally.
 
• They are commonly found in areas where water infiltrates at higher elevations and flows down to regions with impermeable rock layers.
 
• Examples include the Great Artesian Basin in **Australia**, one of the largest and most important artesian aquifers globally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Groundwater Recharge:**

 
 
• Artesian aquifers depend on recharge zones where water infiltrates from the surface, often at higher elevations.
 
• These recharge zones are critical for maintaining water pressure and ensuring long-term sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Artesian Aquifers:**
 
 
• They are extensively used for **irrigation**, drinking water supply, and industrial processes.
 
• Natural springs formed from artesian aquifers are often tourist attractions due to their scenic beauty and therapeutic properties.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns:**
 
 
• Over-extraction of water from artesian aquifers can lead to a decrease in pressure and loss of natural spring flow.
 
• Proper management and regulation are essential to protect these resources from depletion and contamination.

questions.question: Generally, what portion of the crop was collected as tax by the state during the Mahajanapada period?
questions.solution:

__
 
• During the **Mahajanapada period**, the state collected a specific portion of the crop as tax from farmers, which was referred to as **Bali**.
 
• The tax collected was generally **1/6th of the total produce**, which was considered fair and sufficient to support the administrative and military needs of the kingdom.
 
• This taxation system was a critical part of the economic structure and ensured the functioning of the state, including the king’s court and public welfare activities.
 
• The tax collection system during the Mahajanapada period was well-organized, and the collected revenue was used for **state administration, defense, and development projects**.
 
• Farmers were expected to pay taxes in the form of agricultural produce, as the economy during this era was primarily agrarian.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahajanapada Period:**

 
 
• The Mahajanapada period marks a significant phase in Indian history, roughly around the 6th century BCE.
 
• There were **16 Mahajanapadas**, including kingdoms like Magadha, Kosala, and Vatsa, which were prominent political entities.
 
• The economy during this era was predominantly **agrarian**, with trade and commerce also playing an essential role.
 
 
 
• **Taxation System:**
 
 
• Taxes were crucial for the functioning of the state and were collected from farmers in the form of a portion of their agricultural produce.
 
• This system ensured a steady revenue for the administration and supported activities such as **infrastructure development** and maintenance of the army.
 
 
 
• **Social Structure:**
 
 
• Society during the Mahajanapada period was divided into various classes based on occupation, including farmers, traders, warriors, and priests.
 
• The taxation system was designed to be equitable, ensuring that the burden was shared among different sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The collection of 1/6th of the produce as tax is mentioned in ancient texts like the **Arthashastra** and other historical documents.
 
• This system was considered fair and sustainable, allowing the state to meet its needs without overburdening the farmers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **King’s Role:**

 
 
• The king was responsible for ensuring the welfare of his subjects and utilized tax revenue for public works, defense, and maintaining law and order.
 
• He was also tasked with protecting agricultural activities and ensuring the farmers’ prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Economic Sustainability:**
 
 
• The collection of 1/6th of the produce as tax was designed to balance the needs of the state and the farmers.
 
• It allowed farmers to retain a significant portion of their produce for personal use and trade.

questions.question: During the Raja festival, womanhood is celebrated. In which Indian state is this festival extremely popular?

__
 
• **Raja Festival** is a popular festival celebrated in the Indian state of **Odisha**. It is one of the most well-known festivals in the region.
 
• The festival is dedicated to **womanhood** and specifically celebrates **fertility and menstruation**, which is considered sacred and vital for human life.
 
• It is a **three-day festival** that marks the beginning of the agricultural season and is celebrated with great enthusiasm and traditional fervor.
 
• The term "**Raja**" is derived from the Sanskrit word "**Rajas**," meaning menstruation. It is believed that during this time, Mother Earth undergoes a period of rest and rejuvenation, similar to a menstruating woman.
 
• During this festival, women are treated with respect, and they refrain from cooking or performing household chores as a symbol of rest and rejuvenation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Celebration of Raja Festival:**

 
 
• The festival is celebrated in the **month of June**, coinciding with the arrival of the **monsoon season**.
 
• It is also known as "**Raja Parba**" or "**Mithuna Sankranti**" in Odisha.
 
• During the festival, swings (locally called "**Dolies**") are hung from trees, and women enjoy swinging on them as part of the festivities.
 
• Special dishes such as "**Poda Pitha**" (baked rice cake) and other traditional delicacies are prepared and shared among family members and neighbors.
 
• Women wear new clothes, apply **alatha** (a red dye applied to the feet), and participate in folk songs and dances.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Raja Festival:**
 
 
• The festival signifies the **sacredness of womanhood** and acknowledges the importance of menstruation as a natural process vital for life.
 
• It also marks the **agricultural significance**, as it is believed that Mother Earth menstruates during these three days and prepares herself for the upcoming agricultural season.
 
• The fourth day of the festival is known as "**Vasumati Snana**," when women bathe the grinding stone (symbolizing Mother Earth) with turmeric paste and water.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian States:**
 
 
• **Kerala:** Known for its prominent festivals like **Onam** and **Vishu**. It does not celebrate Raja Festival.
 
• **West Bengal:** Celebrates festivals such as **Durga Puja** and **Poush Mela**, but Raja Festival is not significant in this state.
 
• **Maharashtra:** Famous for **Ganesh Chaturthi** and **Gudi Padwa**, but does not have any cultural or traditional association with Raja Festival.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Raja Festival is a unique celebration of **femininity** and **nature**, emphasizing the interconnectedness between the two.
 
• It highlights the cultural values and traditions of **Odisha**, making it an integral part of the state's identity.
 
• Through this festival, the community also acknowledges and respects the **biological processes** of women, offering a break from their daily responsibilities.
 
• The festival also brings families and communities together, strengthening **social bonds** through shared traditions and joyful celebrations.

questions.question: The Partition of Bengal was implemented by which British official?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Curzon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Partition of Bengal** was implemented by **Lord Curzon**, the then Viceroy of India, on **16 October 1905**.
 
• The partition was carried out with the objective of dividing Bengal into two provinces: **Eastern Bengal and Assam** and **Western Bengal**.
 
• It was officially justified by the British government on administrative grounds, citing Bengal's vast size and population as reasons for improved governance.
 
• The real motive behind the partition was to **weaken the nationalist movement** in Bengal by dividing the region along **religious lines**—Hindus in the west and Muslims in the east.
 
• The partition led to widespread protests and was eventually annulled in **1911** due to the strong opposition from Indian nationalists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lord Curzon:**

 
 
• Lord Curzon served as the **Viceroy of India** from **1899 to 1905**.
 
• He introduced several reforms, including the **Calcutta Corporation Act** and **Indian Universities Act**, but his tenure is most remembered for the controversial **Partition of Bengal**.
 
• He believed in strong imperial control and was criticized for his policies that favored British interests over Indian welfare.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Partition:**
 
 
• The partition led to the emergence of the **Swadeshi Movement**, which encouraged Indians to boycott British goods and promote indigenous industries.
 
• It united Indians across regions, religions, and communities, fostering a stronger sense of nationalism.
 
• While the British aimed to divide Hindus and Muslims, the partition inadvertently strengthened nationalist sentiments against colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Protests and Annulment:**
 
 
• The partition faced significant opposition from leaders like **Rabindranath Tagore** and **Surendranath Banerjee**, who rallied people through protests, songs, and literature.
 
• On **12 December 1911**, the British government annulled the partition, citing administrative inefficiency and nationalist resistance.
 
• The capital of India was shifted from **Calcutta** to **Delhi** in the same year.
 
 
 
• **Religious Divide:**
 
 
• The partition exacerbated religious divisions between Hindus and Muslims, which later became a significant factor in India's struggle for independence.
 
• It laid the foundation for communal politics that continued to affect Indian society in the years leading up to partition in **1947**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other British Officials:**

 
 
• **Lord Minto:** Served as Viceroy of India from **1905 to 1910**. He is known for the **Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)**, which introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
 
• **Lord Mountbatten:** The last Viceroy of India, oversaw India's independence and partition in **1947**.
 
• **Lord Wellesley:** Served as Governor-General of India from **1798 to 1805**. He is known for implementing the **Subsidiary Alliance** system.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Partition of Bengal marked a turning point in India's struggle for independence, as it galvanized people to fight against British imperialism.
 
• It highlighted the British strategy of "divide and rule," which sought to weaken Indian unity.
 
• Understanding the partition is crucial to comprehending the socio-political dynamics that shaped India's journey to independence.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution instructs the State to ensure the right to work, education and public assistance in specific circumstances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 41**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 41** of the Constitution of India falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV of the Constitution).
 
• It specifically instructs the State to make provisions for securing the **right to work, education, and public assistance** in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement, and in other cases of undeserved want.
 
• Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court but are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• **Article 41** emphasizes the responsibility of the State to ensure social and economic justice to its citizens.
 
• The provisions under Article 41 aim to reduce inequalities and promote welfare measures for disadvantaged sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• DPSPs are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution under Articles 36 to 51.
 
• They are inspired by the **Irish Constitution** and are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts.
 
• The objective of DPSPs is to establish social and economic democracy and welfare in the country.
 
 
 
• **Article 38:**
 
 
• It directs the State to strive to promote the welfare of the people by securing and protecting a social order in which **justice, social, economic, and political, shall inform all institutions**.
 
 
 
• **Article 45:**
 
 
• Originally, Article 45 aimed to provide free and compulsory education for children up to the age of 14 years within ten years of the Constitution's adoption.
 
• It was later amended by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002**, which made elementary education a fundamental right under Article 21A.
 
 
 
• **Article 48:**
 
 
• It directs the State to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines and to preserve and improve breeds and prohibit the slaughter of cows and calves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Directive Principles** act as guidelines for the government to frame laws and policies aimed at achieving socio-economic justice.
 
• Although not enforceable, they are fundamental for governance and the State is expected to apply them in its administration.
 
• The courts have upheld the importance of DPSPs in various judgments, stating that they are as significant as Fundamental Rights in guiding government policies.
 
• While **Article 41** specifically deals with the right to work, education, and public assistance, other articles like **39, 42, 43** complement it by addressing related issues like health, equal pay, and living wages.
